def cluster_predictions(data, eps=1.0, min_samples=2):
    """
    Perform DBSCAN clustering on the time segments
    eps: maximum distance between two samples (in seconds)
    min_samples: minimum number of samples in a cluster
    """
    df = pd.DataFrame([{
        'start_time': pred['segment'][0],
        'end_time': pred['segment'][1],
        'label': pred['label'],
        'score': pred['score']
    } for pred in data])

    # Use the middle point of each segment for clustering
    X = np.array([(start + end) / 2 for start, end in zip(df['start_time'], df['end_time'])]).reshape(-1, 1)
    
    # Perform DBSCAN clustering
    clustering = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples).fit(X)
    
    # Add cluster labels to DataFrame

    return df

def process_h3_statistics(gdf_rts_ctr, gdf_aoi, year, LEVEL):
    """
    Process H3 hexagon statistics for RTS data

    Parameters
    ----------
    gdf_rts_ctr : GeoDataFrame
        RTS centroids data
    gdf_aoi : GeoDataFrame
        Area of interest data
    LEVEL : int
        H3 hexagon resolution level
    output_file : Path

    Returns

    None
    """

    gdf_rts_ctr = gdf_rts_ctr[gdf_rts_ctr["year"] == year]
    gdf_rts_ctr["geometry"] = gdf_rts_ctr.centroid

    # filter to selected year
    gdf_aoi = gdf_aoi[gdf_aoi["year"] == year]

    h3_ids = get_h3_ids(gdf_aoi, LEVEL)

        gdf_rts_ctr.h3.geo_to_h3(LEVEL)[["area_m2", "area_ha", "n_unique_dates"]]
        .reset_index(drop=False)
        .groupby(f"h3_{LEVEL:02d}")
        .sum()
        .rename(
            columns={
                "area_m2": "area_m2_sum",
                "area_ha": "area_ha_sum",
                "n_unique_dates": "count",

    mean = (
        gdf_rts_ctr.h3.geo_to_h3(LEVEL)[["area_m2", "area_ha"]]
        .groupby(f"h3_{LEVEL:02d}")

    )

        sum, how="outer"
    )  # .join(mean, how='outer')

    dfh3 = dfh3[~dfh3.index.isin(["0", np.nan])]

    gdfh3["count_km2"] = gdfh3["count"] / gdfh3["h3_cell_area"]

def compute_mle_elo(df, scale=400, base=10, init_rating=1000, ANCHOR=None):

        df[df["winner"] == "model_a"],

def parse_script(raw_script: str, paper_id: str) -> BaseModel:
    """
    Parse raw script text into ArxflixScript model.
    
    Args:
        raw_script (str): Raw script text with \component format
        paper_id (str): ArXiv paper ID
        
    Returns:
        ArxflixScript: Validated script model
    
    Example:
        >>> raw_script = '''
        ... \Headline: Understanding GPT-4
        ... \Text: Welcome to this exciting paper review!
        ... \Figure: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.11273/figure1.png
        ... '''
        >>> script = parse_script(raw_script, "2405.11273")
    """
    lines = raw_script.strip().split('
')
    components = []
    position = 0
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():
            continue
            
        if not line.startswith('\'):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid line format: {line}")
            
        component_parts = line[1:].split(':', 1)
        if len(component_parts) != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid component format: {line}")
            
        component_type, content = component_parts
        components.append(ScriptComponent(
            component_type=component_type,
            content=content.strip(),
            position=position
        ))
        position += 1
    
    title = next((comp.content for comp in components 
                 if comp.component_type == ScriptComponentType.HEADLINE), "")
    
    return generate_model_with_context_check(paper_id)(
        title=title,
        paper_id=paper_id,
        target_duration_minutes=5.0,
        components=components
    )

def reconstruct_script(script: BaseModel) -> str:
    """
    Reconstruct the script text from ArxflixScript model.
    
    Args:
        script (ArxflixScript): Validated script model
        
    Returns:
        str: Formatted script text
    
    Example:
        >>> script = ArxflixScript(
        ...     title="Understanding GPT-4",
        ...     paper_id="2405.11273",
        ...     target_duration_minutes=5.0,
        ...     components=[
        ...         ScriptComponent(component_type="Headline", content="Understanding GPT-4", position=0),
        ...         ScriptComponent(component_type="Text", content="Welcome to this review!", position=1)
        ...     ]
        ... )
        >>> print(reconstruct_script(script))
        \Headline: Understanding GPT-4
        \Text: Welcome to this review!
    """

'.join(f"\{comp.component_type.value}: {comp.content}"

def get_relevant_papers(query, papers):
    # model = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
    model = SentenceTransformer("dunzhang/stella_en_400M_v5", trust_remote_code=True)
    
    # Embed the query
    query_embedding = model.encode([query])[0]

    # Embed the papers' titles and abstracts
    paper_embeddings = []
    for paper in papers:
        combined_text = paper['title'] + " " + paper['abstract']
        embedding = model.encode([combined_text])[0]
        paper_embeddings.append(embedding)

    # Calculate cosine similarity
    similarities = cosine_similarity([query_embedding], paper_embeddings).flatten()

    # Get top K most relevant papers
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(similarities)[::-1]
    # add the score to the paper dict
    sorted_papers = [{**papers[id], 'score': similarities[id]} for id in sorted_indices]

    return sorted_papers

def parse_markdown_to_queries(markdown_file):
    """
    Parse a markdown file to extract queries, categories, filter queries, and score thresholds.
    
    Args:
        markdown_file (str): Path to the markdown file.
    
    Returns:
        list: List of dictionaries containing the extracted information.

    queries = []

        lines = file.readlines()
    
    current_query = {}
    for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("# "):
            if current_query:
                queries.append(current_query)
            current_query = {"id": line[2:]}
        elif line.startswith("query ="):
            current_query["query"] = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip().strip('"')
        elif line.startswith("category ="):

        elif line.startswith("score_th ="):
            current_query["score_th"] = float(line.split("=", 1)[1].strip())

    """
    Parse raw script text into ArxflixScript model.
    
    Args:
        raw_script (str): Raw script text with \component format
        paper_id (str): ArXiv paper ID
        
    Returns:
        ArxflixScript: Validated script model
    
    Example:
        >>> raw_script = '''
        ... \Headline: Understanding GPT-4
        ... \Text: Welcome to this exciting paper review!
        ... \Figure: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.11273/figure1.png
        ... '''
        >>> script = parse_script(raw_script, "2405.11273")
    """
    lines = raw_script.strip().split('
')
    components = []
    position = 0
    
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip():
            continue
            
        if not line.startswith('\'):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid line format: {line}")
            
        component_parts = line[1:].split(':', 1)
        if len(component_parts) != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid component format: {line}")
            
        component_type, content = component_parts
        components.append(ScriptComponent(
            component_type=component_type,
            content=content.strip(),
            position=position
        ))
        position += 1
    
    title = next((comp.content for comp in components 
                 if comp.component_type == ScriptComponentType.HEADLINE), "")
    
    return ArxflixScript(
        title=title,
        paper_id=paper_id,
        target_duration_minutes=5.0,
        components=components
    )

        "limit": 1

class FeatureTransformation:
    """
    Represents a transformation that can be applied to a pd.Series.

    def __init__(self, name="", funcs=None):
        """
        Initializes a FeatureTransformation instance.
        :param name: Name of the transformation.
        :param funcs: List of (func_name, kwargs) to apply in order.
        """
        self.name = name

        self._format_funcs()

            assert isinstance(kwargs, dict), "kwargs must be a dictionary"

    def _format_funcs(self):
        """
        Formats the funcs attribute to ensure it is a list of (func_name, kwargs).
        """
        formatted_func = []
        if isinstance(self.funcs, str):
            formatted_func = [(self.funcs, {})]
        elif isinstance(self.funcs, list):
            # funcs must be a list of (func_name, kwargs)

                    func, kwargs = elt
                    kwargs = {} if kwargs is None else kwargs
                    assert isinstance(func, str) and isinstance(kwargs, dict)
                    formatted_func.append((func, kwargs))

        for func_name, _ in formatted_func:
            assert func_name in FUNCS, f"Unknown function name: {func_name}"
        self.funcs = formatted_func
        logger.debug(f"Formatted funcs are : {self.funcs}")

    def transform(self, s, at=None):

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

def discretize(value: float, discretization_multiplier: float) -> int:
    """Discretize incoming value by multiplying and casting to int

    Args:
        value (float): input value
        discretization_multiplier (float): what to multiply by

    Raises:
        ValueError: negative values or negative multipliers

    Returns:
        int: discrete int
    """
    if discretization_multiplier <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"Discretization multiplier <= 0: {discretization_multiplier}")
    return int(value * discretization_multiplier)


def undiscretize(value: int, discretization_multiplier: int) -> float:
    """Undiscretizes a value from a discretized space.

    Args:
        value (int): discrete value
        discretization_multiplier (int): multiplier for the discretization

    Returns:
        float: undiscrete float
    """
    if discretization_multiplier <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"Discretization multiplier <= 0: {discretization_multiplier}")
    return value / discretization_multiplier


class RobotState(BaseModel):
    x: float = Field(0, description="X position of the robot")
    y: float = Field(0, description="Y position of the robot")
    heading: float = Field(0, description="Orientation of the robot in degrees")
    speed: float = Field(0, description="Forward driving speed in m/s")

    def apply_action(self, action: "RobotAction"):
        # Update speed and heading
        self.speed += action.acceleration
        self.heading += action.steer
        self.heading %= 360
        if self.heading < 0:
            self.heading += 360

        # Convert heading to radians for trigonometry
        heading_radians = math.radians(self.heading)

        # Update x and y based on speed and heading
        self.x += self.speed * math.cos(heading_radians)
        self.y += self.speed * math.sin(heading_radians)


class RobotAction(BaseModel):
    acceleration: float = Field(..., description="Robot acceleration measured in m/s^2")
    steer: float = Field(..., description="Change in robot heading measured in degrees")

    @staticmethod
    def random_action() -> "RobotAction":
        """Generates random actions to be used for testing the simulation engine

        Returns:
            RobotAction: Randomly generated action
        """
        return RobotAction(
            acceleration=random.uniform(
                constants.MAX_ROBOT_ACCELERATION,
                constants.MAX_ROBOT_ACCELERATION
                + constants.ROBOT_ACCELERATION_DISCRETIZATION_MUTIPLIER,
            ),
            steer=random.uniform(
                constants.MAX_STEER,
                constants.MAX_STEER + constants.ROBOT_STEER_DISCRETIZATION_MUTIPLIER,
            ),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def action_space_shape() -> NDArray[np.int64]:
        """
        Returns:
            NDArray[np.int64]: Shape of the action space to be used in gym environment
        """
        return (
            [
                discretize(
                    constants.MAX_ROBOT_ACCELERATION,
                    constants.ROBOT_ACCELERATION_DISCRETIZATION_MUTIPLIER,
                )
                + 1,
                discretize(
                    constants.MAX_STEER, constants.ROBOT_STEER_DISCRETIZATION_MUTIPLIER
                )
                + 1,  # action spaces are exclusive of max, +1 to account for this
            ],
        )

    def undiscretize(self, environment_action: NDArray[np.int64]):
        """Goes from discrete action space to floating point values

        Args:
            environment_action (NDArray[np.int64]): Array of acceleration and steer in discrete integers given by the environment
        """
        self.acceleration = undiscretize(
            environment_action[0], constants.ROBOT_ACCELERATION_DISCRETIZATION_MUTIPLIER
        )
        self.steer = undiscretize(
            environment_action[1], constants.ROBOT_STEER_DISCRETIZATION_MUTIPLIER
        )

class Observation(ABC):

class StaticObservation(Observation):
    @staticmethod
    def observation_space_shape() -> NDArray[np.int64]:
        return [
            int(constants.MAP_WIDTH),  # distance to left wall

            int(constants.MAP_LENGTH),  # distance to top wall
            int(constants.MAP_LENGTH),  # distance to bottom wall
        ] + (

                int(

                int(constants.MAX_OBSTACLE_WIDTH),  # obstacle width
                int(constants.MAX_OBSTACLE_LENGTH),  # obstacle length

            * constants.NUMBER_OF_MAP_OBSTACLES
        )

    @staticmethod
    def calculate_observation(
        state: "State", robot_state: RobotState
    ) -> tuple[NDArray[np.int64], pd.DataFrame]:

        discrete_map_observation = [int(x) for x in map_observation]

        # Combine map and obstacle observations into discrete observations
        discrete_observation = discrete_map_observation + discrete_observation

        # Create a DataFrame with labels for each type of observation (walls and obstacles)
        # Label rows to distinguish between "wall" and "obstacle" entries
        observation_labels = ["wall"] * 4 + [
            "obstacle"
        ] * constants.NUMBER_OF_MAP_OBSTACLES

        # Organize data into a DataFrame-friendly structure
        wall_data = [

            [map_observation[1], 0, constants.MAP_WIDTH, 0],  # Right wall

            [0, map_observation[3], 0, constants.MAP_LENGTH],

        # Split obstacle data into rows for the DataFrame
        obstacle_data = [

        )

        obs_shape = StaticObservation.observation_space_shape()
        assert all(
            0 <= obs < bound for obs, bound in zip(discrete_observation, obs_shape)
        ), f"StaticObservation: Observed value {discrete_observation} is out of the bounds {obs_shape}"

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class FunctionInfo:
    """Classe pour stocker les informations d'une fonction."""

    name: str
    description: str


@dataclass
class FileInfo:

class FunctionVisitor(ast.NodeVisitor):
    """Visiteur AST pour extraire les informations des fonctions."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.functions = []

    def visit_FunctionDef(self, node: ast.FunctionDef):
        """Visite chaque définition de fonction dans l'AST."""
        # Extraction de la docstring
        docstring = ast.get_docstring(node) or "Pas de description disponible"

        function_info = {
            "function_name": node.name,
            "function_description": docstring.strip(),
        }

        self.functions.append(function_info)

        # Continue la visite pour les fonctions imbriquées
        self.generic_visit(node)


def analyze_python_file(file_path: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
    """Analyse un fichier Python et retourne les informations sur ses fonctions."""
    try:
        with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
            content = file.read()

        # Parse le contenu en AST
        tree = ast.parse(content)

        # Visite l'AST pour extraire les informations
        visitor = FunctionVisitor()
        visitor.visit(tree)

def cluster_predictions(video_id: str, predictions: List[Dict], eps=1.0, min_samples=2):
    """
    Perform DBSCAN clustering on the time segments for a single video
    """
    df = pd.DataFrame([{

        'start_time': pred['segment'][0],

    df['cluster'] = clustering.labels_
